references.text: The same offering for one who cannot afford a lamb: two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
Shows the option for the poor who cannot afford doves, illustrating the principle of giving according to one's ability.
The same provision of two turtledoves or two young pigeons for a woman who cannot afford a lamb after childbirth.
Repeats the same offering of turtledoves or young pigeons in the cleansing ritual: one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
Two turtledoves or two young pigeons for cleansing from discharge, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
The same offering for a woman with discharge: two turtledoves or two young pigeons for a sin offering and a burnt offering.
The Nazirite shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
Joseph and Mary brought this offering at Jesus' presentation in the temple, showing that they were poor and followed the Law of Moses.
